paper_metadata.title: High-Gain SiGe Transimpedance Amplifier Array for 10 Gb/s Parallel Optical-Fiber Link a 12
paper_metadata.abstract: A transimpedance amplifier array for 12 parallel optical-fiber channels each operating at 10 Gb/s is presented, which is used in the receiver of short-distance links. It stands out for the following features: high gain (transimpedance 25 k in the limiting mode), high input sensitivity and wide input dynamic range (input current swing from 20 to 240 A ), – constant output voltage swing (differential 0.5 V at 50 load), – and low power consumption (1.4 W) at a single supply voltage Fig. 1. Simplified block diagram of a parallel optical-fiber link with the (5 V). Each channel has its own offset-current control circuit. transimpedance amplifier array presented in this paper. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, the total throughput of 10 Gb/s = 120 Gb/s is the highest value reported for a 12 single-chip amplifier array. The target specifications have been Transmitter and receiver modules with 12 channels and data achieved with the first technological run without needing any rates up to 3.4 Gb/s per channel have just been put on the market redesign. Now the problems of such high-gain amplifier arrays can reliably be solved question arises: can the data rate per fiber be further increased, by applying adequate decoupling measures and simulation tools. e.g., up to 10 Gb/s, at reasonable costs? figures.caption: Fig. 4. Simplified circuit diagram of the amplifier cell in Fig. 3. (a) First cell. (b) Second and third cells. In the first cell, a transimpedance state (TIS) without emitter followers in the feedback path is chosen because of its lower group delay variation at high frequencies. In the second and third cells, an emitter follower (EF) is used in the feedback path of the TIS to simplify dc biasing of the succeeding stages. The additional EF pair in the second and third cells steepens the pulse edges.
